title: TriAgent: Divergence-Aware Multi-Agent Routing for Cost-Efficient LLM Inference
description:
TriAgent is a divergence-aware multi-agent routing framework that reduces large language model inference cost by routing each query to the cheapest model tier that can answer it correctly. It stratifies agents by contextual granularity — a word-level lexicon, a sentence-level domain transformer, and a cross-sentence LLM reasoner — and uses the pairwise disagreement between them, the Semantic Divergence Index (SDI), as an unsupervised routing signal.

The same signal serves two further purposes at zero marginal cost: it keys a multilingual semantic cache in which 95% of Chinese queries are answered from an English cache at F1 0.99, and it acts as a post-hoc LLM hallucination detector at ROC AUC 0.898.

The central empirical finding is the critic plateau: an LLM re-tasked as a critic over the cheaper agents' outputs reaches macro-F1 0.87 at 1.5B, 3B, and 7B alike, with overlapping bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. A same-size three-persona vote collapses to 0.66, identifying granularity-stratified diversity rather than multi-agent voting as the mechanism. The plateau is calibration-conditional and fails where the mid-tier specialist is miscalibrated; that failure case is reported in full.

This repository reproduces every number in the paper.
notes: Accepted as a short paper at CIKM 2026 (Rome, 7-11 November 2026). An earlier version received the Long Oral Paper Award at the FinLLM workshop at IJCAI 2026. The paper is published open access under CC BY 4.0; this code is MIT licensed.
